name: Example: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve
problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=e^t, y=2e^{2t}.$ Calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t) = e^t, \qquad y'(t)=4e^{2t}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{4e^{2t}}{e^t} = 4e^t.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(4{e}^{t})}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{t}}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
